headline: Iranian envoys meet Qatari mediators as threat looms of US strikes after midterms
description: Qatari mediators proposed seven-day US-Iran trust-building plan, official says
author: Reuters
article_text:
Iranian negotiators held talks in ​Doha with Qatari mediators on Saturday to discuss paths out of war in the Gulf, a source told Reuters, as diplomats ‌try to avert a new outbreak of fighting after the US midterm elections this week.

Saturday’s talks in the Qatari capital followed more than 12 hours of discussions on Friday between Iranian and Qatari envoys in Tehran, said the source, who was briefed on the negotiations and spoke on condition of anonymity. The source said the talks were ​being coordinated in regular contact with Washington.

Countries in the region have been anticipating that US President Donald Trump, who has held off ​on strikes on Iran during the weeks leading up to Tuesday’s midterm elections, could restart attacks once the ⁠voting is over. Iran has repeatedly said it would respond to new attacks by striking at US and Israeli targets in neighbouring countries.

Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah ​Mojtaba Khamenei issued a statement on Saturday ordering the armed forces to be prepared to respond to any attacks. The Iranian military later announced it was taking steps to ​improve its readiness.

“Any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful, and geographically unrestricted response,” Khamenei, who has not appeared in public since replacing his father, killed at the war’s outset, said on Saturday in the statement posted on his official Telegram account.

He said that senior commanders had reported high readiness along the ​Gulf coast, in and around the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf of Oman, and on Iran’s northwestern and southeastern borders.

Diplomacy continues despite gaps

Trump, who ​launched the war alongside Israel in February, has repeatedly hinted at plans to restart strikes on Iran. Last week he called on Israelis ahead of their own election ‌to keep ⁠his wartime ally Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in power so the two leaders can “finish the job”.

But Washington has also lately taken steps to indicate it is open to diplomacy. Earlier this week, Vice President JD Vance, who led the US delegation at previous rounds of talks with Iran, wrote a letter to a hardline senior Iranian security official, which the New York Times and Wall Street Journal described as an initiative to see if it ​was possible to restart talks.

Trump played ​the letter down, saying he approved ⁠it only to discuss the possibility of letting more medical supplies into Iran: “I said if you want to do that, that’s ok. Basically, it’s getting supplies in to help people that are not well.”

In the latest Qatari-mediated discussions, ​the Qataris brought a proposal to Tehran a week ago for a seven-day plan, under which the US and Iran would ​take daily steps to ⁠build trust ahead of broader peace talks, the source briefed on the negotiations said. A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Friday that this proposal was not deemed satisfactory by Tehran.

Iran has been proposing its own seven-day plan since September, so far rejected by Trump. That calls for Washington to lift a blockade ⁠of Iranian ​ports, unfreeze assets and approve an Iranian-backed route through the Strait of Hormuz, after which ​the contested strait would be reopened.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said in remarks reported by Al Jazeera on Saturday that Iran was studying Vance’s letter. He said the Iranian plan was the ​only proposal on the table to reopen the strait.

headline: Zaman blitz powers Pakistan to clinch tri-nation ODI title
description: Fakhar Zaman and Saad Baig put on 149-run partnership after Pakistan lose two early wickets in tri-series final
author: Reuters
article_text:
Fakhar Zaman’s superb century powered Pakistan to a three-wicket victory over Sri Lanka in the One-Day International tri-series final in Lahore on Saturday, ending the hosts’ long wait for the title.

Zaman’s 127 off ​99 balls anchored the chase after an early wobble, while Salman Agha provided crucial support ‌before Arafat Minhas’ half-century paved the way for victory.

Pakistan chased down a target of 326, finishing on 331 with nine balls to spare to complete the joint-highest successful chase in an ODI final.

Earlier, Sri Lanka posted a formidable 325 for eight ​wickets, built around Kamindu Mendis’ outstanding 131 off 128 balls and a fluent 77 from Pavan ​Rathnayake.

The pair shared a crucial 146-run partnership before Pakistan struck late to curb ⁠any hopes of a 340-plus surge, with Shaheen Shah Afridi taking two wickets for 50 runs.

The victory ​secured Pakistan’s first ODI tri-series title since 2008, when they beat India in the Kitply Cup final in ​Bangladesh, and made amends for their defeat to New Zealand in the final of a home tri-series in 2025.

Pakistan suffered early setbacks as Dilshan Madushanka struck twice in the powerplay, including the prized wicket of Babar Azam for a five-ball duck.

​Zaman and Saad Baig rebuilt the innings with an impressive 149-run partnership, and Baig brought up his maiden ​ODI fifty before Maheesh Theekshana ended his knock for 74 off 75 balls.

Zaman accelerated after reaching his half-century and went ‌on ⁠to register his 12th ODI century, partnering with Agha in a brisk 57-run stand that kept Pakistan firmly on course in the chase.

The left-hander eventually fell to Madushanka, followed soon by Agha for 17, leaving Pakistan at 230-5.

However, Minhas’ and Hasan Nawaz’s 94-run partnership ultimately carried the hosts to the target.

Sri Lanka ​made a strong start after ​being put in to ⁠bat, with opener Avishka Fernando and Kamindu Mendis adding 51 runs in the powerplay. Fernando’s dismissal in the 18th over ended the opening stand, and Pakistan struck ​again soon after when captain Kusal Mendis fell to Agha, leaving the visitors ​at 109-2.

Kamindu ⁠and Rathnayake steadied the innings with a fluent 146-run partnership off 119 deliveries. The stand kept Sri Lanka firmly in control until Kamindu, who brought up his maiden ODI century, fell after hitting 12 fours and two sixes.

Pakistan ⁠fought back ​in the death overs, triggering a collapse as Afridi and ​Haris Rauf removed Dasun Shanaka and Rathnayake within the space of two overs.

Sahan Arachchige provided a late cameo with a brisk 15 ​off 12 deliveries before falling to Naseem Shah.

headline: Rezaei: No decision made to change nuclear doctrine
description: Tehran says its conditions for negotiations remain unchanged amid efforts to revive talks
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Iran has made no official decision to change its nuclear doctrine despite calls from some lawmakers and members of the public to reconsider its position if war resumes, Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei has said.

Rezaei said neither the government nor the Supreme National Security Council had formally decided to alter the country’s nuclear policy, according to remarks carried by the semi-official Tasnim News Agency.

He said calls for a change had emerged following attacks on Iranian nuclear facilities despite extensive inspections and the installation of online monitoring cameras by the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA).

Rezaei also revealed that a new letter delivered to Iran’s Foreign Ministry through American intermediaries had undergone an initial review, but Tehran had yet to respond.

“The noticeable change in the tone of this letter compared with previous correspondence demonstrates the consolidation of the Iranian nation’s power and victory,” he said.

He stressed that Iran’s seven conditions remained unchanged, adding that they included additional demands that had brought the total to more than seven.

Rezaei said negotiations on other issues, including Iran’s nuclear commitments and continued membership of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), could take place in a second phase, provided the country’s nuclear rights were fully recognised.

He argued that more than two decades of extensive IAEA inspections, along with numerous documents and reports, demonstrated the peaceful nature of Iran’s nuclear activities.

On the Strait of Hormuz, Rezaei said Iran’s conditions established its role in managing the shared waterway, with all maritime traffic passing under Iranian supervision.

The remarks come amid efforts to revive negotiations between Washington and Tehran, with Qatar and Pakistan leading mediation efforts.

Reports have indicated progress in indirect talks in Doha as the two sides seek understandings on Iran’s nuclear programme, sanctions and maritime security in the strait.

The Wall Street Journal previously reported, citing US officials, that Vice President JD Vance had sent a message to Rezaei at President Donald Trump’s direction in an effort to revive peace talks.

Trump denied the report, saying Vance’s role was limited to helping provide medical supplies needed by Iran.

headline: Germany’s Gen Z protests turn violent as stores looted in Frankfurt
description: Protesters demand better education, lower living costs and end to compulsory military service
author: Reuters
article_text:
Hooded rioters looted stores in Frankfurt late on Saturday after tens of thousands of demonstrators ​took to the streets across Germany’s biggest cities to demand better education and lower living costs.

The protests followed a wave of Gen Z-led ‌demonstrations across Europe this year.

In Serbia, student-led activism helped unseat the country’s longtime leader at the ballot box, while protests in France have descended into rioting and looting.

The German protests organised by the campaign group “Gen Z regelt” — “Gen Z takes charge” in German — took place in 34 cities including Berlin, Frankfurt and Munich.

The group says it opposes compulsory military service and wants greater investment in education, as many ​young Germans struggle with rising costs.

In Frankfurt, Germany’s financial hub, at least two stores were looted as protests turned violent, with several more damaged and ​police trying to get the situation under control, according to a Reuters witness.

“Violent disturbances are continuing,” Frankfurt police said on X.

“In ⁠the city centre, windows have been smashed at several shops. Molotov cocktails are also being thrown at the emergency services. We urge all bystanders to avoid the ​city centre or to leave the area.”

Official numbers on Saturday afternoon suggested turnout was below the 182,000 participants that organisers initially expected.

Police in Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin ​reported as many as 18,000 protesters, half the roughly 36,000 on the organisers’ website.

German authorities said Saturday’s demonstrations, which coincide with Halloween festivities, had been largely peaceful, but warned of attempts by extremist groups to exploit the movement.

In Hamburg, some barricades had been set on fire.

“We are here today to fight for peace and freedom, rather than for war and coercion,” Gen Z regelt spokesperson Lina ​Friedrich said in Berlin on Saturday.

“What matters most to us is better support for the health and education systems. We are against compulsory military service, and we ​are in favour of a fairer distribution of the burden.”

Luxury shops board up windows

Parts of Germany’s far-left extremist scene and some groups linked to foreign extremist movements have joined efforts to ‌mobilise support, ⁠according to the federal interior ministry.

“We all have those images from France in our minds — looting, burning houses, burning police vehicles, and attacks on police officers,” said Roman Poseck, interior minister for the state of Hesse, whose capital is Germany’s financial hub, Frankfurt.

“France must not be held up as a model in this regard.”

Some businesses across German cities boarded up windows and planned early closures ahead of the demonstrations due to concerns over possible unrest, including along Berlin’s luxury Kurfuerstendamm shopping boulevard.

Organisers have focused on what ​they see as the growing pressure on ​younger generations in Europe’s largest economy.

“The ⁠government has offered no response to our concerns other than to continue making cuts and piling further burdens upon us,” said Steve, an 18-year-old due to speak at a rally in Munich, addressing Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

“We will continue to exercise our fundamental ​right to assemble until you stop ignoring us.”

Germany has struggled to revive economic growth. The country also faces growing pressure on pensions ​and public services as ⁠baby boomers retire and the working-age population shrinks.

Questions have been raised about who is driving the campaign and whether it is genuinely youth-led, given the broad mix of political and civil society groups involved.

Germany’s national school student umbrella organisation, BSK, has distanced itself from the initiative and plans to hold a separate day of protest on November 20.

Sean Baker, ⁠a student at ​the Technical University of Berlin, said he would join the protests on Saturday to call attention ​to the poor state of buildings on campus.

“When you go inside and enter the rooms, it looks like an abandoned building,” he told Reuters. “Yet this is where we’re expected to study on a regular basis.”

article_html:
Hooded rioters looted stores in Frankfurt late on Saturday after tens of thousands of demonstrators ​took to the streets across Germany’s biggest cities to demand better education and lower living costs.

The protests followed a wave of Gen Z-led ‌demonstrations across Europe this year.

In Serbia, student-led activism helped unseat the country’s longtime leader at the ballot box, while protests in France have descended into rioting and looting.

The German protests organised by the campaign group “Gen Z regelt” — “Gen Z takes charge” in German — took place in 34 cities including Berlin, Frankfurt and Munich.

The group says it opposes compulsory military service and wants greater investment in education, as many ​young Germans struggle with rising costs.

In Frankfurt, Germany’s financial hub, at least two stores were looted as protests turned violent, with several more damaged and ​police trying to get the situation under control, according to a Reuters witness.

“Violent disturbances are continuing,” Frankfurt police said on X.

“In ⁠the city centre, windows have been smashed at several shops. Molotov cocktails are also being thrown at the emergency services. We urge all bystanders to avoid the ​city centre or to leave the area.”

Official numbers on Saturday afternoon suggested turnout was below the 182,000 participants that organisers initially expected.

Police in Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin ​reported as many as 18,000 protesters, half the roughly 36,000 on the organisers’ website.

German authorities said Saturday’s demonstrations, which coincide with Halloween festivities, had been largely peaceful, but warned of attempts by extremist groups to exploit the movement.

In Hamburg, some barricades had been set on fire.

“We are here today to fight for peace and freedom, rather than for war and coercion,” Gen Z regelt spokesperson Lina ​Friedrich said in Berlin on Saturday.

“What matters most to us is better support for the health and education systems. We are against compulsory military service, and we ​are in favour of a fairer distribution of the burden.”

Luxury shops board up windows

Parts of Germany’s far-left extremist scene and some groups linked to foreign extremist movements have joined efforts to ‌mobilise support, ⁠according to the federal interior ministry.

“We all have those images from France in our minds — looting, burning houses, burning police vehicles, and attacks on police officers,” said Roman Poseck, interior minister for the state of Hesse, whose capital is Germany’s financial hub, Frankfurt.

“France must not be held up as a model in this regard.”

Some businesses across German cities boarded up windows and planned early closures ahead of the demonstrations due to concerns over possible unrest, including along Berlin’s luxury Kurfuerstendamm shopping boulevard.

Organisers have focused on what ​they see as the growing pressure on ​younger generations in Europe’s largest economy.

“The ⁠government has offered no response to our concerns other than to continue making cuts and piling further burdens upon us,” said Steve, an 18-year-old due to speak at a rally in Munich, addressing Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

“We will continue to exercise our fundamental ​right to assemble until you stop ignoring us.”

Germany has struggled to revive economic growth. The country also faces growing pressure on pensions ​and public services as ⁠baby boomers retire and the working-age population shrinks.

Questions have been raised about who is driving the campaign and whether it is genuinely youth-led, given the broad mix of political and civil society groups involved.

Germany’s national school student umbrella organisation, BSK, has distanced itself from the initiative and plans to hold a separate day of protest on November 20.

Sean Baker, ⁠a student at ​the Technical University of Berlin, said he would join the protests on Saturday to call attention ​to the poor state of buildings on campus.

“When you go inside and enter the rooms, it looks like an abandoned building,” he told Reuters. “Yet this is where we’re expected to study on a regular basis.”

headline: Trump says US still has one or two targets to strike in Iran
description: Trump identifies Pickaxe Mountain as potential target but says US is not in a hurry to act
author: AFP
article_text:
US President Donald Trump has said American forces have severely weakened Iran’s military capabilities but still need to deal with one or two remaining targets, including a suspected underground nuclear facility known as Pickaxe Mountain.

Trump said negotiations with Iran to end the war, launched by the US and Israel in late February, were progressing, although he questioned Tehran’s reliability.

“We’ve knocked out their nuclear. We still have to take care of, I would say one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes,” Trump told reporters at his Florida residence on Saturday.

Referring to the suspected underground nuclear complex, he added that Pickaxe Mountain was among the sites that still needed to be dealt with, saying the US could act against the targets quickly.

“You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, and you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly,” he added, referring to a suspected underground nuclear complex.

Iran has denied conducting any nuclear activities at the site.

Trump reiterated that Washington was in no hurry to launch further offensive operations, arguing that US strikes had already decimated Iran’s military and nuclear programme.

Earlier on Saturday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump had not made a decision on fresh strikes against Iran, adding that Washington remained open to a diplomatic solution.

Meanwhile, Iran’s supreme leader warned the United States and Israel against launching further attacks, following threats of renewed military action after the US midterm elections.

Trump has previously indicated that he was weighing further military action after the elections, saying he was considering whether to “finish them off”.

headline: Zardari, Shehbaz felicitate Gilgit-Baltistan on Independence Day
description: Leaders pay tribute to those who fought against Dogra rule and secured region’s freedom
author: Web Desk
article_text:
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif have congratulated the people of Gilgit-Baltistan on their 79th Independence Day, paying tribute to those who fought against Dogra rule to secure the region’s freedom.

In separate messages on Sunday, both leaders recalled the historic struggle 79 years ago, when the people of Gilgit-Baltistan overthrew Dogra rule, declared independence and subsequently sent a letter to Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah seeking accession to Pakistan.

President Zardari said the people of Gilgit-Baltistan had made valuable contributions to Pakistan’s defence and development.

Prime Minister Shehbaz paid tribute to the determination, courage and sacrifices of the region’s leaders and people in achieving freedom.

He reaffirmed the federal government’s commitment to extending full support to the Gilgit-Baltistan government in addressing economic challenges and introducing institutional and administrative reforms.

headline: India tightens security ahead of big opposition march in Delhi
description: Rahul Gandhi will lead march against voter list changes, demand election chief’s resignation
author: Reuters
article_text:
Indian security personnel carrying batons and shields and accompanied by riot control vehicles surrounded the site of a planned opposition protest in Delhi on Sunday that is set to ​demand the resignation of the country’s election chief over a controversial revision of voter lists.

headline: Binance to resume withdrawals after recovering 95% of stolen crypto
description: Exchange says withdrawals will restart in phases as it works to recover remaining assets
author: Reuters
article_text:
Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, said it would resume withdrawals in phases after covering ​95% of the $6.3 billion in tokens stolen ‌from its platform in the world’s largest digital heist, which the FBI has tied to North Korea.

Binance said ​the phase would start on Sunday and include bitcoin, ether, BNB, ⁠Solana, XRP, dogecoin and other tokens.

The remaining ​5% of stolen tokens consists of assets that are ​less liquid and may take longer to source in the required amounts, Binance posted on X late on Saturday.

The FBI ​said on Saturday the North Korean state-sponsored unit ​known as TraderTraitor was responsible for the attack.

Pyongyang has for ‌years ⁠denied using state-linked cyber units for espionage, financial theft and revenue.

Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not respond to requests ​for comment.

Members of ​the unit ⁠were observed by law enforcement converting stolen assets into the cryptocurrency Ethereum, ​the FBI said in a statement, adding ​that ⁠it expects “further laundering” of the assets through the use of related technology.

headline: Judge ends Trump's attempts to sue Wall Street Journal over Epstein reporting
description: Federal judge rules president failed to establish actual malice in the newspaper’s reporting
author: Reuters
article_text:
A US federal court has dismissed US President Donald Trump’s second attempt to sue the Wall Street Journal over its reporting on his ties to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, dealing another setback to his defamation case.

The US District Court for the Southern District of Florida on Saturday ruled that Trump had again failed to demonstrate actual malice, a legal requirement for public figures pursuing defamation claims.

“As with his first attempt, he has failed,” Judge Darrin P. Gayles wrote in the ruling.

Gayles highlighted what he described as the newspaper’s “thoughtful and detailed investigation” and noted that its reporters had sought comments from Trump and other officials before publishing the report.

“Grasping at straws, the Amended Complaint attempts to manufacture flaws with the investigation,” the judge wrote.

Trump’s lawyers had argued that the newspaper should have abandoned the story after the president denied any involvement with Epstein.

However, Gayles rejected the argument, saying it did not meet the legal standard for actual malice and ran contrary to the First Amendment.

Trump had refiled the lawsuit in May, seeking at least $10 billion in damages over the newspaper’s reporting.

The latest dismissal was issued with prejudice, meaning Trump cannot bring the same case before the court again.

headline: Trump calls $50m contract for ex-lawyer 'not acceptable'
description: Alina Habba Mildon secured the four-year deal while serving at the Justice Department
author: Reuters
article_text:
US President Donald Trump has said it was “unacceptable” for one of his former lawyers, Alina Habba ​Mildon, to secure a $50 million contract for herself while working ‌at the US Department of Justice.

“I thought it was totally obnoxious and outrageous, and it’s not acceptable,” Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida, on Saturday. “Not ​acceptable at all.”

The New York Times reported last week that the ​family of Julio Herrera Velutini, a Venezuelan banker facing US felony ⁠bribery charges before striking a plea deal in August 2025, guaranteed ​Habba Mildon more than $50 million over four years.

The deal, according to the ​newspaper, would pay $10 million a year plus bonuses.

Trump said he told Habba Mildon he did not want her to be paid and called the episode “terrible.”

Habba Mildon was serving as the ​acting US attorney in New Jersey when she signed the contract with ​Herrera’s family company, Concord Partners, days after it was registered in late October 2025, ‌the ⁠New York Times reported.

By the time she started her employment with the Herrera family, a court had disqualified her from serving as US attorney.

She resigned on December 8 and was appointed a senior adviser to the attorney general ​the same day, ​and was still ⁠in that role when, according to the New York Times, she started at Concord on January 1.

Trump pardoned Herrera ​on January 15, 2026, according to the Justice Department’s ​website.

Habba Mildon ⁠last week said she was never paid for a pardon, never met with anyone at the White House or Justice Department about a pardon, and never ⁠did ​any work for a pardon for anyone.

The ​Justice Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

headline: UN employee dies after two years in Houthi custody
description: Yemen holds Houthis responsible as UN rights chief demands probe into Al Shami's death
author: Web Desk
article_text:
A United Nations employee has died in Houthi custody after more than two years of abduction and enforced disappearance in Yemen, the country’s human rights minister has said.

Human Rights Minister Mashdal Mohammed Omar announced the death of Mohammed Ibrahim Al Shami, an employee of the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, in a statement posted on X on Saturday.

Omar said Al Shami had spent more than two years in Houthi custody, during which his family was denied visits and any contact with him.

He held the Houthis responsible for the employee’s abduction, enforced disappearance and death, adding that the circumstances surrounding his death remained unknown and his body had not been handed over to his family.

The minister said the case highlighted the need for stronger international efforts to monitor the conditions of detained UN personnel and secure their release.

He called for an investigation into Al Shami’s death, the immediate handover of his body to his family and accountability for those responsible.

He also urged more effective measures to secure the release of others being held in detention.

UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk described Al Shami’s death as a “heartbreaking loss”, saying it followed more than two years of arbitrary detention.

In remarks shared by the UN human rights office on X, Türk said Al Shami’s family had received no explanation about the cause or circumstances of his death and deserved to know the truth.

He called for an urgent, full and independent investigation and urged the immediate and unconditional release of all other detained UN personnel.

The Houthis have not commented on the minister’s statement.

headline: Israelis urge opposition to join forces with Arab parties to oust Netanyahu
description: Demonstrators call for an alliance that could give anti-Netanyahu bloc a 67-seat majority
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Hundreds of Israelis took to the streets in Tel Aviv and Jerusalem on Saturday, urging the opposition to form an alliance with Arab-majority parties to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has stepped up his attacks on the minority group’s leaders.

Arab-majority parties made significant gains in Tuesday’s election, driven by anger over rhetoric targeting their community from Netanyahu’s radical government.

However, opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has yet to decide whether to seek a coalition with them.

At a rally in Tel Aviv, Ayelet Raz said the Arab community, which makes up around 20% of Israel’s population, had the right to political participation.

“It’s the last chance for real change,” the 60-year-old psychologist said, describing Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, as a “great manipulator”.

“We need to give peace a chance,” she said. “Otherwise we’ll have this bloodshed forever.”

Inconclusive election results

Tuesday’s election produced no clear winner, with neither bloc securing a majority in Israel’s 120-seat parliament.

Jewish-majority parties opposed to Netanyahu won 48 seats, while the two Arab-majority parties, Raam and the Joint List, secured a combined 19 seats.

An alliance between the two camps could give the anti-Netanyahu bloc a comfortable majority of 67 seats, although some opposition parties oppose the arrangement.

Around 500 protesters in Tel Aviv carried placards reading “Arabs and Jews will only win together” and “There is a majority for change”.

In Jerusalem, where around 100 people gathered, signs included “67 — United we stand, divided we get Bibi” and “Why not, really — unless we are racist?”

Arab parties have formally joined an Israeli government only once, when Raam leader Mansour Abbas became part of a short-lived coalition that governed from 2021 to 2022.

Abbas has indicated he would be willing to join another government.

Yousef Jabareen of the Joint List, meanwhile, told AFP he was prepared to support Eisenkot in parliament without joining his government, citing concerns including the war in Gaza.

Eisenkot, 66, a former military chief and political newcomer, broadly shares Netanyahu’s security positions, including on Gaza, which Israel has devastated since the October 7, 2023, attacks.

On Saturday, he reiterated that he would only form a “Zionist government” whose members recognise Israel as a “Jewish, democratic and liberal state” and Hamas as a “terrorist organisation”. Arab leaders have previously rejected these conditions.

Although Eisenkot has said he does not want a government dependent on Arab parties, he has not explicitly ruled out relying on their support from outside the coalition.

Yair Golan, leader of the left-wing Democrats, has strongly backed the prospect of a government supported by Arab parties, arguing that excluding them would be racist. He also met Abbas on Thursday.

However, Avigdor Liberman, head of the right-wing anti-Netanyahu Yisrael Beiteinu party, has ruled out joining a coalition that relies on Arab parties, even for support from outside the government.

“Whoever wants to rely on supporters of terrorism, let them. Yisrael Beiteinu will not be there,” he wrote on Facebook on Friday.

More than 100 Netanyahu supporters staged a counter-protest alongside the Tel Aviv rally, chanting “It’s the Right, or Palestine”, a slogan used during the prime minister’s election campaign.

President Isaac Herzog is expected to give a party leader a mandate to form a government within 28 days by Thursday, with a possible 14-day extension.

The coalition negotiations are unfolding as Netanyahu and US President Donald Trump have hinted at a possible new attack on Iran, a development that could allow the Israeli premier to delay political manoeuvring until fresh elections.

headline: Bangladesh forms wage board as garment workers continue protests
description: Thousands demand more than double the current pay, with rallies disrupting factories
author: Reuters
article_text:
Bangladesh announced a six-member wage board on Sunday to review garment workers’ pay and urged employees to return to work, but ​protests demanding higher wages continued across major industrial areas, disrupting transport ‌and factory operations.

Workers in the South Asian nation are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka ($245), more than double the current 12,500 taka, saying rising costs of food, housing, transport and ​healthcare have sharply eroded their purchasing power.

The dispute has raised concerns about ​disruption to an industry that employs about 4 million workers, generates more ⁠than 80% of Bangladesh’s export earnings and supplies clothing to many leading Western ​brands.

Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury said the wage board was formed after ​discussions with workers’ representatives and industry leaders and urged workers to resume work.

Despite the announcement, thousands of garment workers staged fresh demonstrations on Sunday.

Police used tear gas and water cannon to disperse ​workers who had blocked a busy intersection in Dhaka, police said. Some protesters hurled ​bricks at officers during the clashes.

Hundreds of workers also blocked a major highway in Gazipur, on ‌the ⁠outskirts of the capital, disrupting transport in one of the country’s key industrial belts.

The demonstrations forced owners to shut 25 to 30 factories, while authorities deployed Border Guard Bangladesh personnel to maintain order, Gazipur Industrial Police Superintendent Mohammad Amjad Hossain said.

The latest ​unrest follows demonstrations in ​Ashulia, a major ⁠garment manufacturing hub on the outskirts of Dhaka, where dozens of factories suspended operations on Saturday after workers staged protests demanding ​higher pay.

Chowdhury warned that prolonged disruptions could delay export shipments ​and payments ⁠from international buyers, creating further difficulties for manufacturers and workers alike.

Bangladesh’s ready-made garment industry, the world’s largest after China, contributes about 10% of gross domestic product and is the ⁠backbone of ​the economy.

Manufacturers, however, said the sector is facing mounting ​challenges, including rising production costs, periodic gas and electricity shortages, and uncertainty in energy markets linked to tensions ​in the Middle East.

headline: Trump administration steps up poll pressure ahead of midterms
description: Justice Dept. intensifies probe into Alaska Senate race and signals appeal over mail-in ballots
author: Reuters
article_text:
President Donald Trump’s administration pressed a criminal investigation into Alaska’s pivotal US Senate race and said on Saturday it would ​likely take its fight over thousands of California mail-in ballots to the Supreme Court, as the midterm campaign for control of Congress entered its final weekend.

In Alaska, federal prosecutors are investigating ‌whether aides to Democratic challenger Mary Peltola helped to recruit a retired schoolteacher, Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., to run because his name is similar to the Republican incumbent, Senator Dan S. Sullivan.

The closely contested race is seen as crucial to Democrats’ hopes of taking the Senate in Tuesday’s vote.

It is one of 35 Senate races, along with all 435 House seats, that will decide whether Trump’s Republicans keep control of Congress for his final two years in office.

Republicans hold a 53-47 Senate majority and a narrow ​edge in the House.

Early voting has set a record. More than 51 million Americans have already cast ballots in person or by mail, according to the University of Florida’s Election Lab, up ​from nearly 46 million who voted before Election Day at the last midterms in 2022.

In California, a federal appeals court this week ruled 2-1 that the ⁠Justice Department had failed to justify its emergency bid to force the state to set aside mail ballots from more than 20,000 registered voters it alleges are likely noncitizens.

“I hesitate to give a final answer, but ​I think probably the Supreme Court’s next on this one,” acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter told Fox News on Saturday, adding that any request for Supreme Court consideration would come before Tuesday’s election.

Trump has been ​on a campaign blitz in multiple states over the past month but is spending Saturday at his Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida. He returns to the campaign trail on Sunday in Kansas and Iowa.

Alaska probe intensifies

The Justice Department’s top prosecutor in Alaska, US Attorney Michael Heyman, said at a Friday press conference that a recent New York Times article, saying there had been an effort to recruit Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. had driven a “surge” of FBI resources onto the case.

Heyman said he had ​assigned several prosecutors to it and that investigative steps were taking place “intensely and swiftly.”

Peltola and the campaign committee have denied involvement in any effort to recruit the second Sullivan.

The retired teacher has denied coordinating with ​Peltola’s campaign.

Voters in Alaska have largely dismissed the fight over the ballot.

“I knew which Dan Sullivan was which Dan Sullivan, you know? It’s very clear on the ballot,” Anchorage resident Mickey Buster, 36, said as he stood outside a ‌polling place on ⁠Saturday.

But another Anchorage voter, Carol Riggs, 52, said she was disappointed by the entire situation and the possibility it “muddies the water for some voters, potentially.”

Michigan rift

In Michigan, where Democrat Abdul El Sayed faces Republican Mike Rogers in another closely watched Senate race, El Sayed’s feud with the rival he beat in the primary, US Representative Haley Stevens, flared again.

El Sayed’s campaign asked Stevens to skip his events through Election Day so as “not to distract from the central issues of the campaign,” a person familiar with the matter said.

Stevens has backed El-Sayed but demanded he condemn an outside group’s ad blaming Israel for high grocery prices and apologise for past rhetoric about Israel.

“It’s certainly ​unhelpful to the El-Sayed campaign to have continued visible ​division within the party just before Election Day,” ⁠said Matt Grossmann, a political scientist at Michigan State University. Polls show El Sayed has largely consolidated Democratic support.

Trump’s pressure campaign

The administration, beyond its bid to block the counting of ballots from more than 20,000 California voters it alleges could be noncitizens, has sued roughly 30 states and the District of Columbia seeking unredacted voter ​rolls.

The legal manoeuvres have alarmed state election officials. Under the Constitution, states have primary authority over how elections are run.

On Friday, a federal judge ordered the Justice ​Department to stop threatening to prosecute ⁠California election officials who defy its directives.

California Governor Gavin Newsom, a Democrat, on Saturday warned the state’s top federal judges that the Justice Department may seek warrants to seize ballots before results are certified, though he said he did not know of any pending request.

Newsom said in a letter to the judges that the only reason to seize ballots “would be to interfere” in the count.

Sean Morales-Doyle of the Brennan Centre for Justice said the efforts, while ⁠unlikely to ​win in court, aim at “creating uncertainty, sowing fear, distrust, chaos,” in hopes of pressuring officials such as Alaska’s lieutenant governor “to do something ​that they’re not supposed to do.”

Even so, 76% of US voters are confident their ballots will be counted accurately, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted from September 30 to October 5, with confidence about equally high among Republicans and Democrats.

In Alaska, federal prosecutors are investigating ‌whether aides to Democratic challenger Mary Peltola helped to recruit a retired schoolteacher, Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., to run because his name is similar to the Republican incumbent, Senator Dan S. Sullivan.

The closely contested race is seen as crucial to Democrats’ hopes of taking the Senate in Tuesday’s vote.

It is one of 35 Senate races, along with all 435 House seats, that will decide whether Trump’s Republicans keep control of Congress for his final two years in office.

Republicans hold a 53-47 Senate majority and a narrow ​edge in the House.

Early voting has set a record. More than 51 million Americans have already cast ballots in person or by mail, according to the University of Florida’s Election Lab, up ​from nearly 46 million who voted before Election Day at the last midterms in 2022.

In California, a federal appeals court this week ruled 2-1 that the ⁠Justice Department had failed to justify its emergency bid to force the state to set aside mail ballots from more than 20,000 registered voters it alleges are likely noncitizens.

“I hesitate to give a final answer, but ​I think probably the Supreme Court’s next on this one,” acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter told Fox News on Saturday, adding that any request for Supreme Court consideration would come before Tuesday’s election.

Trump has been ​on a campaign blitz in multiple states over the past month but is spending Saturday at his Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida. He returns to the campaign trail on Sunday in Kansas and Iowa.

The Justice Department’s top prosecutor in Alaska, US Attorney Michael Heyman, said at a Friday press conference that a recent New York Times article, saying there had been an effort to recruit Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. had driven a “surge” of FBI resources onto the case.

Heyman said he had ​assigned several prosecutors to it and that investigative steps were taking place “intensely and swiftly.”

Peltola and the campaign committee have denied involvement in any effort to recruit the second Sullivan.

The retired teacher has denied coordinating with ​Peltola’s campaign.

Voters in Alaska have largely dismissed the fight over the ballot.

“I knew which Dan Sullivan was which Dan Sullivan, you know? It’s very clear on the ballot,” Anchorage resident Mickey Buster, 36, said as he stood outside a ‌polling place on ⁠Saturday.

But another Anchorage voter, Carol Riggs, 52, said she was disappointed by the entire situation and the possibility it “muddies the water for some voters, potentially.”

El Sayed’s campaign asked Stevens to skip his events through Election Day so as “not to distract from the central issues of the campaign,” a person familiar with the matter said.

Stevens has backed El-Sayed but demanded he condemn an outside group’s ad blaming Israel for high grocery prices and apologise for past rhetoric about Israel.

Even so, 76% of US voters are confident their ballots will be counted accurately, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted from September 30 to October 5, with confidence about equally high among Republicans and Democrats.

headline: Shehbaz calls Pakistan’s G-24 chairmanship a diplomatic milestone
description: PM Shehbaz says the role will strengthen Pakistan’s voice in global economic affairs
author: APP
article_text:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Sunday termed Pakistan’s election as chairman of the Intergovernmental Group of Twenty-Four (G-24) an important diplomatic milestone, stating it would further strengthen the country’s voice and role in global economic affairs.

According to a spokesperson, the prime minister, expressing deep pleasure over the achievement, commended Finance Minister Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb and the entire Ministry of Finance team for their tireless efforts, effective diplomacy, and professional capabilities.

He appreciated the finance minister and his team for their proactive role during the annual meetings of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF), noting that their efforts helped secure a prominent position for Pakistan in providing economic leadership to developing nations.

The prime minister said the G-24 chairmanship would provide Pakistan with an influential platform to advocate for essential reforms in the global financial system, ensure equitable financial assistance to combat climate change, and foster sustainable development opportunities for emerging economies.

headline: Govt revises petrol pricing formula amid Iran-US tensions
description: Refineries told to surrender price differentials to govt; financial benefit to be passed on to consumers
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The federal government has revised the petrol pricing mechanism amid tensions between Iran and the United States, directing oil refineries to implement a new formula approved by the federal cabinet.

In letters issued to refineries, the Petroleum Division outlined the revised mechanism, which was approved by the cabinet on Friday, Business Recorder said in a report.

Under the new formula, petrol’s import price will be determined based on the actual import cost of the relevant Pakistan State Oil (PSO) cargo.

If the actual cost is unavailable when daily prices are calculated, the premium, additional costs and customs duty applicable to the last available cargo will be used as the benchmark.

The revised mechanism allows refineries to calculate petrol’s ex-refinery price over the next 30 days by keeping the premium, incidentals and customs duty at the levels prevailing on March 7, 2026, before the war began.

Refineries will be required to surrender the difference between the import price calculated under the first provision and the ex-refinery price determined under the second to the government under the Petroleum Levy account head C03901.

The financial benefit resulting from this adjustment will be passed on exclusively to motor spirit (MS), or petrol, consumers through a corresponding reduction in retail prices.

To ensure implementation of the cabinet’s decision, all refineries have been directed to deposit the differential petroleum levy in accordance with the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority’s (OGRA) price notifications and petroleum levy notifications issued from time to time.

Refineries will also be required to submit daily reports of domestic petrol sales, along with CPRs and payment challans, to the Petroleum Division and OGRA for verification and reconciliation.

headline: Gilgit-Baltistan celebrates Independence Day with patriotic fervour
description: Ceremonies held to pay tribute to freedom fighters who liberated region from Dogra rule
author: APP
article_text:
The 79th Independence Day of Gilgit-Baltistan was celebrated across all 10 districts on Sunday with traditional enthusiasm, patriotic spirit and renewed commitment to the ideals of freedom and accession to Pakistan.

The day began with special prayers in mosques for the peace, prosperity and progress of the country and for the eternal peace of the departed souls of martyrs.

A 21-gun salute was also presented in the morning under the auspices of the Pakistan Army to mark the historic occasion.

The main ceremony was held at the historic Chinar Bagh in Gilgit, where Gilgit-Baltistan Governor Syed Mehdi Shah was the chief guest.

Chief Minister Haji Amjad Hussain, the Force Commander Northern Areas, senior civil and military officials, families of martyrs and a large number of citizens also attended the ceremony.

The Governor hoisted the national flag, while smartly turned-out contingents of police and security forces presented a salute.

Later, the governor, chief minister and force commander visited the Martyrs’ Memorial, laid floral wreaths and offered Fateha to pay tribute to the heroes who sacrificed their lives for the liberation of Gilgit-Baltistan from the Dogra rule on November 1, 1947.

Addressing the gathering, Governor Mehdi Shah paid rich tribute to the freedom fighters and martyrs, saying that the courage and sacrifices of their forefathers had enabled the people of Gilgit-Baltistan to live in freedom.

He said the victory against Dogra rule was the result of the historic struggle and supreme sacrifices of local heroes.

Highlighting the role of the Pakistan armed forces, the governor said that the country’s armed forces had always responded effectively to enemy aggression and foiled hostile designs.

Referring to the recent Pakistan-India military confrontation, he stated that Pakistan’s armed forces had shot down more than seven Indian aircraft during the clashes.

He said the armed forces had always given a befitting response to aggression, safeguarding the country’s security and enabling people to sleep peacefully in their homes.

Chief Minister Amjad Hussain said the brave people of Gilgit-Baltistan had overthrown the oppressive Dogra regime despite limited resources and subsequently taken the historic decision to accede to Pakistan.

He said the sacrifices and spirit of patriotism of their forefathers would continue to inspire future generations.

Another impressive ceremony was held at Helipad Ground Jutial, where Governor Syed Mehdi Shah was the chief guest. Contingents of the Pakistan Army, Gilgit-Baltistan Scouts, police and other security institutions presented an impressive march past and military parade.

Students from various schools and colleges presented national songs and tableaux highlighting the historic freedom struggle of Gilgit-Baltistan, which were warmly applauded by the audience.

headline: Five killed in fresh ethnic violence in India's Manipur state
description: Three Kuki men die in gunfight, two others found dead after going missing earlier
author: Reuters
article_text:
Five people were killed in two separate incidents in India’s northeastern state of Manipur, police said on ​Sunday, as fresh ethnic violence erupted in the conflict-hit region.

Three ‌men from the Kuki tribal group were killed in an exchange of gunfire between “unidentified armed miscreants” in the state’s Noney district on Saturday, according to a police ​statement.

The bodies of two other men from the same community, ​who had gone missing earlier this week, were recovered in ⁠Kangpokpi district on Sunday morning after security personnel launched a search ​operation, a second police statement said.

A top Kuki tribal body blamed Naga ​separatist outfits for the killings, describing them as a “direct unprovoked assault … in their homeland.”

The killings came amid mass protests attended by hundreds of thousands of people in ​the state capital Imphal and other areas, demanding the abrogation of ​a ceasefire arrangement between Kuki armed groups and the Indian state.

The predominantly Christian Kuki ‌and ⁠Naga tribes have a long history of conflict over competing claims to ethnic homelands in the remote northeastern state.

The latest fighting erupted after a Naga man was allegedly assaulted by men from the Kuki community ​in February this ​year.

The killing ⁠of three Kuki pastors in May, allegedly by Naga armed groups, triggered a series of retaliatory abductions and ​killings by both sides.

The latest Kuki-Naga clashes have added ​to tensions in ⁠Manipur, where the Kuki community is also embroiled in a bloody ethnic conflict with the mainly Hindu Meitei community that began in May 2023 over ⁠economic ​benefits and job quotas.

More than 60,000 people ​displaced by the conflict, which has claimed more than 300 lives, continue to live in ​temporary shelters.

headline: Qatari LNG tanker attacked in Gulf waters: State media
description: No crew members injured in the attack on Al Mayeda, which remains operational
author: AFP
article_text:
A Qatari liquefied natural gas (LNG) tanker was attacked with “unidentified objects” while sailing through Gulf waters, Qatar’s state news agency reported on Sunday.

The incident occurred on Friday evening and involved Al Mayeda, a vessel owned by the Qatar Gas Transport Company, the Qatar News Agency (QNA) said.

No crew members were injured in the attack, and there was no environmental impact, according to the report.

The Qatari company said the vessel remained in a safe condition and was operational following the incident.

The vessel attack comes amid escalating tensions in the Gulf, with Iran targeting marine vehicles in the Strait of Hormuz and the wider Gulf in an effort to assert control over maritime traffic.

Tehran has maintained that ships must seek its permission to pass through the strategic waterway. Qatar, which has been mediating in the conflict, has intensified diplomatic efforts in recent days to revive negotiations between the United States and Iran.

headline: Next war could last longer than previous conflict: Iran
description: Army spokesperson says Trump will not dictate timing or terms of any future clash
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Iran has warned that any future conflict with the United States could last longer than the previous war, saying US President Donald Trump would not be able to dictate its duration or the terms of its conclusion.

“A potential future war could last longer than the previous conflict, and the American president would not be in a position to dictate the timing or the conditions of its conclusion,” army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said on Sunday, according to Iranian state television.

He was referring to the most intense phase of the war that began on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, killing the Islamic Republic’s supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

headline: Thousands protest in Delhi, demand resignation of election chief
description: Congress-led demonstrators accuse the election commission of voter list manipulation
author: Reuters
article_text:
Thousands protested in Delhi on Sunday to demand the resignation of India’s election chief over a revision of voter lists, the latest in more than a month of opposition demonstrations challenging Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Led by Congress party chief Rahul Gandhi, Sunday’s protesters say the controversial revision benefits Modi’s Hindu radical Bharatiya ​Janata Party.

Analysts say the protests and growing support for the opposition form the worst crisis for Modi since he came to ​power in 2014, though his government remains stable and the next general election is not due until 2029.

Authorities ⁠tightened security and warned of traffic diversions before protesters began a march from central Delhi to the designated rally site, where the ​opposition has predicted hundreds of thousands of people would participate.

Calls for accountability

Hundreds of security personnel, some of them carrying batons ​and shields and accompanied by riot-control vehicles, surrounded the historic Ramlila Maidan ground as hundreds of people, many waving national and party flags, began moving towards it.

Opposition party leaders led the march in an open-top jeep.

Among the thousands waiting for the marchers at the Ramlila Maidan was Reena Mahto, a member ​of the Congress’ student wing, who said four people from her family had been deleted from the voter list due to the ​false claim that they had moved elsewhere.

She told Reuters the family has long lived in Jagdalpur in the central state of Chhattisgarh, but “now all of ‌a sudden ⁠we have been marked as shifted from our own house,” adding, “There should be accountability, and we are here to seek that.”

The change to voter rolls removed over 130 million names — more than the population of Japan.

Opposition parties allege the deletions disproportionately affected Muslim voters and other minorities, who are unlikely to support the BJP.

The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol, while the ​BJP has accused rivals of trying ​to undermine democracy by wrongly ⁠questioning legitimate electoral processes.

Dinesh Singh said he was joining the protest for the sake of his children’s future.

“I am not affiliated with any political party,” he said. “I am here for a cause. I want ​the children to remember that we fought for their future.”

Minister sees conspiracy

Health Minister Jagat Prakash ​Nadda, however, called ⁠the protest a “carefully orchestrated drama”.

“What is unfolding today at Ramlila Maidan is not an act of respect for democracy. It is a calculated conspiracy to plunge the nation into anarchy, all in the name of democracy,” he told news agency ANI.

The demonstration is the latest in a series ⁠of near-daily protests ​that opposition parties, student organisations and the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party have held since late September ​demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

The protests erupted after the Indian Express newspaper reported that Kumar’s two deputies had raised several concerns internally about voter list ​revisions, registration procedures and digital systems.

headline: Iranian negotiators in Doha to continue talks to end the US-Iran war, official says
description: Diplomatic efforts gather pace even as Tehran prepares for possible attacks and Trump leaves door open to renewed military action
author: Reuters
article_text:
Iranian negotiators were in Doha on Sunday for a third consecutive day of talks with Qatari mediators ​aimed at pushing for a deal to end the ‌US-Israeli war on Iran, an official briefed on the discussions told Reuters.

The talks come amid concerns that the conflict could escalate again ​after the November 3 US midterm elections. President Donald ​Trump has said the United States will not launch ⁠new attacks on Iran before the vote and that ​talks with Tehran have been productive, though he has not ​ruled out further military action thereafter.

Iran has repeatedly said it would respond to any new attacks by striking US and Israeli targets in ​neighbouring countries, as the eight-month-old war continues to disrupt global ​oil supplies and spill over across the Middle East.

Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah ‌Mojtaba ⁠Khamenei issued a statement on Saturday ordering the armed forces to be prepared to respond to any attacks. The Iranian military later announced it was taking steps to improve its ​readiness.

US Secretary ​of State Marco ⁠Rubio said on Saturday that Trump has not decided whether to launch new strikes against ​Iran, but would prefer to resolve the ​conflict diplomatically.

Qatari ⁠mediators were in Tehran on Friday for discussions with Iranian officials before moving the talks to Doha on Saturday, an ⁠official ​told Reuters. The talks were being ​coordinated in regular contact with Washington, the official added.
